answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because island only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, thread is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any ferrous approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
